title: Work authorisation and resident-centred scope
audience: Cleaners and cleaning supervisors who clean in residential aged care, and in other healthcare, NDIS and dental settings, in any Australian state or territory. This is the opening lesson of the healthcare cleaning vertical.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NHMRC, Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) (no page date shown; document dated 2019), which has only been partly confirmed; NDIS worker screening (no date shown); Aged Care Act 2024: news and commencement (no date shown).
learningOutcomes: Explain the difference between environmental cleaning by a cleaner and infection prevention and control decisions made by clinical and IPC staff.
Identify the written authority needed before work starts in a residential aged care or healthcare setting.
Describe how resident dignity, consent and privacy limit where and how a cleaner may work.
State the stop-and-refer triggers and the record that must follow a stop.

instruction.heading: Why this lesson comes first
instruction.body: A cleaner in a residential aged care facility, a clinic, a dental practice or an NDIS setting works in the place where people live, receive care and are most vulnerable to infection. Environmental cleaning is one of the controls that reduce the spread of infection, and the NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (document dated 2019) treat cleaning and spill management as part of preventing transmission from the environment to patients. But cleaning is not clinical care. Decisions about which precautions apply to a resident, which area is restricted, what product may be used near a clinical device, and whether a person has an infection belong to clinical staff and the infection prevention and control team. This lesson explains where the cleaner's authority ends.

instruction.heading: Written authority and the work order
instruction.body: Before you start, you need written authority for the task. A work order or site instruction should name the area, the surfaces or items, the approved product and method, the time window, and the person who gave the direction. A verbal request from a resident, a family member or a visitor is not authority to change the scope, and a request from a colleague does not replace the written list. If the facility's current infection prevention plan or outbreak instruction differs from the work order, follow the current instruction and tell your supervisor. Do not follow the work order where it would be unsafe under the current instruction.

instruction.heading: Resident-centred scope: dignity, consent and privacy
instruction.body: Residents are people in their own home or room, not only locations to be cleaned. A cleaner should knock, introduce themselves, ask before entering personal space, and explain what they will do. Do not move a resident, their belongings or their aids without permission, and do not read, move or photograph personal papers or medical charts. Privacy and dignity are part of the infection prevention approach, because a resident who feels that staff respect them is more likely to accept care. Where a resident refuses, asks you to stop, or appears distressed, stop that part of the task and tell the carer. Do not argue, and do not continue to force access.

instruction.heading: Where the cleaner's authority ends
instruction.body: Cleaning staff do not decide which precautions apply to a resident, do not set or lift isolation, do not give clinical advice, and do not decide that a room may be entered or left when the clinical team has set a restriction. They do not handle body fluids beyond the facility's spill procedure, and they do not handle clinical waste or sharps unless the facility has trained and authorised them to do so. They do not touch clinical devices, change their settings, or clean the interface of a device used on a resident unless the facility authorises that task in writing. When any of these comes up, stop and refer to the clinical team or the IPC contact, and record the referral.

instruction.heading: Licences, screening and the limit of this lesson
instruction.body: Completing this lesson does not give you a licence, a registration, a clearance or an authority to do regulated work. For NDIS settings, the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission states (page with no date shown) that a worker delivering NDIS supports and services may need an NDIS worker screening clearance, and that meeting worker screening obligations is a condition of provider registration. Residential aged care commenced under the Aged Care Act 2024 on 1 November 2025, and the strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards started on the same date (Department of Health news page, no date shown).

procedure: Read the written work order and confirm the area, the items, the product and method, and the time window.
Check the current facility infection prevention notice or outbreak instruction, and confirm the work order is still valid under it.
Confirm any screening or check required for the setting before entering a resident area.
Introduce yourself to the resident or carer, explain the task, and ask before entering personal space.
Confirm you are not being asked to make an infection prevention, clinical or device decision. If you are, stop and refer.
Carry out only the authorised tasks, and stop when a resident, carer or instruction asks you to.
Record the area, the tasks completed, any refused access or stop, the referral made and the time.

workedExamples.situation: A resident in a residential aged care room asks you to wipe the screen of a clinical monitor beside the bed, saying it is dirty and their family will complain.
workedExamples.reasoning: The monitor is a clinical device used on the resident. Cleaning its interface is outside your authority unless the facility has authorised that task in writing. Explain politely that the team will look after the monitor, do not touch it, and tell the carer or nurse. Record the request and the referral. The resident's concern is valid and should be passed on.

workedExamples.situation: On arrival at a clinic, the receptionist says the room you were booked to clean has been restricted by the nurse manager and is not to be entered until the nurse says so.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The clinical team has set a restriction, and cleaning staff do not decide whether a restricted room can be entered. Leave the room, confirm the restriction with the nurse manager, and record the delay and the time. The work is rescheduled under the clinical instruction.

commonErrors.error: Treating a resident's or family member's request as authority to clean a clinical device or change the work order.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the written scope. Refer any device, clinical or change request to the responsible team.

commonErrors.error: Entering a restricted room because it is on the list and the work order looks routine.
commonErrors.prevention: A clinical restriction overrides the list. Confirm with the nurse manager before entering.

commonErrors.error: Moving a resident's aids, belongings or papers to clean underneath them.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not move personal items without permission. Ask the resident or carer.

commonErrors.error: Assuming that a worker's induction or a course completion allows any task in any setting.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the screening, induction and written authority for each setting before work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Cleaning staff do not make infection prevention and control decisions for residents, patients or clients. Decisions on precautions, isolation and restriction are made by clinical staff and the infection prevention team. The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) place environmental cleaning within a wider infection control framework.

Licence notice: For NDIS settings, a worker delivering supports and services may need an NDIS worker screening clearance, and a condition of provider registration is to fulfil worker screening requirements. This lesson does not grant a screening clearance, a licence or any registration. Confirm the requirement for each role.

Residential aged care commenced under the Aged Care Act 2024 on 1 November 2025, and the strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards commenced on the same date. The cleaner's obligation is to follow the facility's procedures under these standards.
Confirm each state and territory before placement.

qualityStandard: The learner states, for three supplied requests, whether the request is within cleaning authority, needs a written change, or must be referred.
The learner describes the steps for entering a resident's room with dignity and consent, without moving personal items.
The learner stops and refers a clinical device request in a supplied scenario, and records the referral.
The learner identifies the screening or check required for a supplied setting, or states that it must be confirmed with the employer.
documentationEvidence: Work order or instruction used, with the area and the authorised tasks
Any refused access, stop or referral, with the person referred to and the time
Confirmation of the screening or check status for the setting
summary: Environmental cleaning is part of infection prevention, but precautions and clinical decisions belong to clinical staff.
Written authority sets your scope. Verbal requests and similar-looking tasks do not extend it.
Dignity, consent and privacy apply to every task. Stop when a resident or carer objects.
Refer clinical device and restriction decisions, and record the referral.

knowledgeChecks.question: A resident asks you to clean the interface of a clinical monitor beside their bed. What is the correct response?
options: Clean it, because the resident asked and it is near the bed, so it is part of the room you clean every day
Clean it with the strongest product you have, so the resident is satisfied and the device looks new to them
Do not touch the device unless the facility has authorised it in writing. Refer to the nurse or carer and record the referral.

knowledgeChecks.question: The clinic nurse manager has restricted a room you were booked to clean. What should you do?
options: Do not enter. Confirm the restriction with the nurse manager and record the delay.
Enter the room, because it is on the booking list for today and the time was set
Enter briefly to check whether the restriction still applies to this room today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about screening for NDIS settings is correct?
options: Completing this lesson gives the screening clearance automatically once the course is finished and signed
A worker delivering NDIS supports may need an NDIS worker screening clearance, which this lesson does not grant.
NDIS settings never require any screening for cleaning staff, whatever their role, hours or location

knowledgeChecks.question: Can a cleaner decide that a room may be entered when the clinical team has set a restriction?
options: Yes, if the room is on the booking list
No, cleaning staff do not decide that a room may be entered when the clinical team has set a restriction
